episode_row: two scheduler units running; orphan respawned after deploys

commits.subject: fix(deploy): self-heal legacy system-level systemd units
commits.body:
Root cause of the orphan-scheduler-after-every-deploy issue:

There were TWO sets of bts systemd units running concurrently:
  - /etc/systemd/system/bts-scheduler.service (system-level, created
    by the original Hetzner setup at 01:08 on April 11)
  - ~/.config/systemd/user/bts-scheduler.service (user-level,
    created at 22:04 on April 11 — the canonical version)

Both had Restart=always with RestartSec=300, so killing one without
the other meant the surviving unit would respawn the dead one
within 5 minutes. The audit just exposed this — every "kill orphan"
was followed by a fresh orphan from the OTHER unit's restart
policy 5 minutes later.

The deploy workflow already restarts the user-level unit only
(`sudo -u bts ... systemctl --user restart`), so the system-level
units have been pure dead weight + race-condition fuel.

Self-heal: on every deploy, check for the legacy system-level
unit file and, if present, disable it, remove it, reload systemd,
and pkill any leftover schedule processes owned by bts. After
the first run on each host this is a no-op.

Also adds .github/workflows/deploy.yml to the deploy path filter
so future workflow edits can deploy themselves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
